findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is still abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the required abstract members counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. Because Detector.detector_handler instantiates group_type.detector_handler(self), any detector with type 'metric_alert_fire' will raise TypeError when processed instead of safely returning no results.

findings.title: get_state_data crashes for stateful handlers with no counters
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.get_state_data only populates counter_updates when self.counter_names is truthy, but then unconditionally accesses counter_updates[gk] for every group key. A stateful handler with no counters (counter_names = []) will raise KeyError as soon as it evaluates a packet with any group key. Use a per-group default empty dict instead.

findings.title: Occurrences are emitted before detector state is committed
findings.body: process_detectors emits occurrences/status changes via create_issue_occurrence_from_result before handler.commit_state_updates() persists dedupe and detector state. If the commit to Redis/DB fails after a successful produce, a retry/reprocessing of the same packet can see the old state and emit duplicate occurrences. This is a data-integrity risk now that stateful detectors produce real occurrences.

findings.title: Docstring still says evaluate returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but the docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. This misdocuments the new contract.

findings.title: get_group_key_values return annotation does not allow None/DetectorGroupKey keys
findings.body: get_group_key_values is annotated as returning dict[str, int], but the rest of the code and tests use DetectorGroupKey keys, including None. The annotation should be dict[DetectorGroupKey, int] (or the actual key type) to match the runtime contract.

findings.title: Test builds expected occurrence for the wrong group key
findings.body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence for group key 'val1' but then evaluates group key 'group_key'. The expected result therefore does not validate the occurrence/fingerprint for the actual group key; the test can only pass if occurrence equality ignores that difference.
